section_summary: This section documents efforts to counter violence and false claims that Japan won the war among Japanese residents of São Paulo state in 1946. Consular officers seek newspapers, photographs, films, broadcasts and handwritten letters from Japan; Massao Kinoshita proposes official clarification and reconciliation. The section also contains lists of proposed correspondents, examples of misleading images, and a Guararapes newspaper account of a public meeting against Shindo Remmei.

subfiles.title: Appeal to Byron S. Lamson
subfiles.about: Kinoshita asks Lamson to help convey the Japanese community’s plight and secure family letters from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses an official appeal and memorial seeking to restore calm among Japanese residents of Brazil.

subfiles.title: Covering appeal to the federal interventor in São Paulo
subfiles.to: Federal interventor in São Paulo state
subfiles.about: Kinoshita submits a memorial on conflict within the Japanese colony.
subfiles.summary: Requests consideration of measures to end terrorism and return the community to work.

subfiles.title: Memorial on the Japanese colony in Brazil
subfiles.to: Federal interventor in São Paulo state
subfiles.about: The memorial analyzes false Japanese victory claims, violence and proposed remedies.
subfiles.summary: Kinoshita argues that forged news and distrust of Japan’s surrender have divided the community and encouraged secret societies and attacks. He urges a joint official declaration authenticating Japan’s surrender notice, handwritten family letters from Japan, and negotiated reconciliation. He also calls for accountability for terrorist acts and renewed agricultural work.

subfiles.title: Reply to Byron S. Lamson
subfiles.from: Daniel M. Braddock, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Lamson’s information on Japanese terrorist activity in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Confirms consular reports and says the Department is assisting Brazilian authorities and Japanese opponents of the violence.

subfiles.title: Telegram on film material for Japanese audiences
subfiles.about: Requests films from the embassy library with Japanese spoken explanations.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Aeronoticias issues for assembly and promises further material.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on 16 mm films
subfiles.about: The embassy requests new films, including footage of the American occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Warns that scarce new film stock threatens a long running exhibition program in workplaces, schools and military bases.

subfiles.title: Japanese situation in São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross reports continued unrest and asks for occupation films.
subfiles.summary: Police arrests have strained capacity; consular officers circulate the emperor’s surrender rescript in Portuguese.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese propaganda postcards
subfiles.about: Cross forwards postcards used to imply that Japan won the war.
subfiles.summary: Reports further shootings and again requests Japanese newspapers and 16 mm footage showing American troops in Japan.

subfiles.title: Correspondence desired from Japan for relatives in São Paulo
subfiles.about: Cross requests expedited handwritten letters from 52 people in Japan to residents of Brazil.
subfiles.summary: A Japanese committee compiled addresses across opposing factions, including detainees. It asks relatives to describe conditions in Japan and acknowledge defeat, with replies routed through the consulate for public use.

subfiles.title: List of proposed Japanese correspondents and recipients
subfiles.about: Lists 52 proposed senders in Japan and recipients in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Five page address list accompanying Despatch 3998, including eight recipients under police arrest.

subfiles.title: Second copy of the 52 person correspondence list
subfiles.about: Reproduces the proposed correspondence pairs from Despatch 3998.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate list of Japanese senders and Brazilian recipients, with minor OCR and typing differences.

subfiles.title: Third copy of the 52 person correspondence list
subfiles.about: Reproduces the correspondence list attached to Despatch 3998.
subfiles.summary: Further copy of the proposed sender and recipient addresses.

subfiles.title: Request to facilitate Japanese family correspondence
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department seeks SCAP help obtaining letters from the listed people in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks that Japanese correspondents be notified and their communications expedited in light of violence in Brazil.

subfiles.title: Japanese in Brazil
subfiles.about: Summarizes violence, false victory claims and the request for family letters.
subfiles.summary: Urges correspondence before ordinary international mail resumes.

subfiles.title: Cross telegram on unrest and deportations
subfiles.about: Cross reports continuing attacks and possible deportations.
subfiles.summary: Estimates fewer than 100 involved and requests transport planning, pictures and films.

subfiles.title: Photographs purporting to show U.S. surrender
subfiles.about: Discusses distributing copies of misleading surrender photographs.
subfiles.summary: Suggests sending sets to officials and MacArthur to obtain better material for Brazil.

subfiles.title: Three Japanese propaganda photographs
subfiles.about: Images and captions misleadingly portray the U.S. surrender ceremony as a Japanese victory.
subfiles.summary: Three photographic examples, with Japanese captions visible on two pages.

subfiles.title: Transmission of photographs indicating U.S. surrender
subfiles.about: Cross explains three misleading photographs circulating among Japanese residents.
subfiles.summary: Describes altered interpretations of images of the USS Missouri, President Truman and armed personnel.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of propaganda photographs
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Cross’s photographs to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Thanks the consulate and hopes the images will prompt useful material for Brazil.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese newsreels and broadcasts
subfiles.about: SCAP is sending Japanese newsreels, radio transcriptions and newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Says shortwave broadcasts from Japan are being considered despite a general overseas broadcast ban.

subfiles.title: Duplicate despatch on surrender photographs
subfiles.about: Repeats the description of three misleading propaganda photographs.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the despatch on fabricated impressions of American surrender.

subfiles.title: Duplicate acknowledgment of photographs
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department’s response to Cross’s photographs.
subfiles.summary: Partial copy of the acknowledgment and referral to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Duplicate telegram on newsreels and broadcasts
subfiles.about: Repeats notice of SCAP newsreels, recordings and newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the June 4 telegram, including the shortwave broadcast issue.

subfiles.title: Cross telegram on correspondence and broadcasts
subfiles.about: Cross stresses the importance of letters from Japan and proposes Tokyo radio broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Also relays a suggestion for a visiting commission including an imperial family member.

subfiles.title: Japanese newspapers sent to São Paulo
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department encloses Japanese newspapers documenting postwar conditions.
subfiles.summary: Lists 21 May 1946 issues of Asahi, Mainichi and Yomiuri.

subfiles.title: Cross telegram acknowledging newspapers
subfiles.about: Cross confirms that recently sent Japanese newspapers will help.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the newspaper supply continue.

subfiles.title: Difficulty securing Japanese papers from the United States
subfiles.about: Cross asks that a ban on mailing U.S. Japanese language papers to Brazil be lifted.
subfiles.summary: Encloses The Rocky Shimpo’s refusal to serve a subscriber in São Paulo.

subfiles.title: The Rocky Shimpo letter to Osamu Ikubo
subfiles.about: The newspaper explains that it cannot yet mail issues to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Returns a subscription payment and promises notice when mailing is authorized.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese newspaper subscriptions
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department reports the end of restrictions on subscriptions to U.S. Japanese papers.
subfiles.summary: Says the restriction ended June 17, allowing subscriptions from Brazil.

subfiles.title: Cross telegram on Wakeyama killing
subfiles.about: Cross reports that four Japanese men killed former Colonel Wakeyama.
subfiles.summary: Links the killing to Wakeyama’s acknowledgment of defeat and urgently requests more newspapers and occupation images.

subfiles.title: Shipment of forty Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department sends a further collection of Japanese papers.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text lists newspaper titles and states that 40 papers are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Shipment of thirty-five Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The Department encloses Japanese vernacular newspapers, many from smaller towns.
subfiles.summary: Lists February 1946 issues and states that 35 copies are enclosed.

subfiles.title: First withdrawal notice
subfiles.about: A notice marks an item withdrawn from the file because access is restricted.
subfiles.summary: Blank withdrawal form; the missing item is unidentified.

subfiles.title: Second withdrawal notice
subfiles.about: A second notice marks an unidentified item withdrawn from the file.
subfiles.summary: Blank withdrawal form; no date or item description is supplied.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Guararapes letter and newspaper article
subfiles.about: Cross encloses a June 13 letter and June 16 article on the Japanese situation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards accounts of a Guararapes meeting addressing Shindo Remmei.

subfiles.title: Translation of Guararapes letter
subfiles.from: José Senoi and Joaquim Yoshio Kamakura
subfiles.about: Community representatives thank the consulate for photographs and describe a public meeting.
subfiles.summary: Reports roughly 400 Japanese attendees, speeches on Japan’s defeat and a pledge to support harmony in Brazil.

subfiles.title: A Cidade de Guararapes article on Shindo Remmei
subfiles.about: The clipping describes a meeting convened to rebut Shindo Remmei’s false victory claims.
subfiles.summary: Local officials and Japanese residents denounce secretive claims that Japan won the war and the extortion and violence tied to them. Speakers urge public verification of news, cooperation with Brazilian authorities and repudiation of Shindo Remmei; attendees pledge to end its activity. The pages include overlapping copies and fragments of the clipping, plus part of a separate food shortage item.
